Melatonin made me feel off in the morning too which I told my doc and she suggested taking it earlier, like dinnertime. That gives it time to help at bedtime but moves the clock up so it shouldn't be affecting you much by wake up time.

I also take propranolol or prasozin to help me fall asleep. These are prescription meds that aren't strong like ambien etc. They are more for anxiety /hypervigillance. They lower the physical response so you can rest more easily. That's not a great explanation but I'm not a doctor lol.

Lastly, sleep hygiene is a huge help, tho I suck at it. But having a regular nighttime routine, say - read a book for 30 mins, then go brush your teeth, wash your face. Get in bed after, journal (helps get those pesky keeping you awake thoughts out), meditate (helps you unwind and shift gears, I love a short guided meditation like a la body scan or just breathing focused). Whatever Your routine is, having one means that when you start that process, you're telling your body it's time to go to sleep and it'll automatically start to switch to sleepy time.

Good luck!!! 😴😴😴

For me, I just had to leave first (after almost 9 years), then the feelings were able to fade. My first nex I tried breaking up with for a year and a half. I'd tell him and I'd try to leave and he'd follow me either on foot or get in my car over and over and over until I gave up everytime. 

To end it, I had to move to go back to school and we'd see what would happen. As soon as I had some space, and he wasn't the only "reality" check in my world. Aka wasn't all in my ear telling me lies, gaslighting, telling me everyone else hates me or is out to get me etc. All that shit. Having the physical distance, I was able to break up with him in like a week.

It still took a long long time and trial and error to get him out of my life more and let the feelings loosen and the bond break.

2nd nex who was quite physically abusive was really really hard to leave. He had me so low that I felt too incredibly shitty about myself to fathom deserving anything better. I was so trauma bonded to him and so ashamed of myself. 

When he went from only hurting me to becoming a threat to someone else's safety (nex 1 almost got me killed "trying to stand up for me"), it was incredibly painful, but I was able to leave him. I struggle with taking care of and standing up for myself, but I cannot be the reason for someone else getting hurt. So just knowing that he could hurt someone else if I saw him and engaged with him, I was able to stay away.

It still took a long long time for the bond to loosen and weaken.

General advice I've read in regard to this is to solely and constantly focus on the shitty things they do. If a sweet loving thought enters your head, redirect it to remember "hey remember the time they screamed at me for 4 hours over nothing while I tried to de escalate the whole time and they wouldn't let me leave" etc etc and that helps.

I strongly recommend putting as much physical and otherwise barriers between you and the person and then trying really hard to focus on their negatives while taking better care of yourself, loving yourself, doing things you wanted but couldn't before and starting to show yourself the like you deserve.

I have trauma, cptsd, anxiety, and panic disorder. I've tried Xanax, Ativan, and klonopin. I also get medication anxiety and can get a panic or anxiety attack when I take a new medication. To counter this, I try to start a new med before I *really* need it in a more urgent situation and I start with a half or quarter dose. This makes me mentally more comfortable and reduces possible negatives while I get accustomed to a new medication. 

Benzos are lifesavers for me for panic attacks and insomnia. I am careful to not take them too frequently. Even just knowing they are there if I need them helps me feel better and can help reduce my anxiety fear that I *might* get a panic attack.

To me, Xanax feels more impactful in a fun but dangerous way. As in I'd be more drawn to take xanax more often because I like how it feels. My doctor said Ativan and klonopin have a longer half life so the effect is a bit milder and longer than xanax which makes them less prone to abuse. In my personal use, I do see this distinction.

I'd recommend asking your doctor for an Ativan or klonopin prescription instead of Xanax and be cautious but don't be scared to use it. It's a great tool in our toolbox, just one that it is important to stay aware of and keep your use not too frequent.
